title: Scene-stored property setters run before the node is in the tree, before its children exist and before @onready
description: When a scene is instantiated the engine creates the native node, attaches the script (member initializers then _init), then calls set() for every stored property, which runs user setters, before the node is added to its parent and before its children are created; @onready vars are still null and is_node_ready() is false, so setters touching child nodes fail; conversely initializer values bypass the setter (derived state computed in setters is skipped for defaults, #86494) and _init cannot see inspector values (#68427).
example: `@export var hp := 1: set(v): hp = v; $Bar.value = v` with hp = 5 stored in the scene -> null-instance error at load
evidence_issues: #68427 (open, 11 reactions, 20 comments: exported fields use default values during _init) | #86494 (closed not planned 2026-09, 12 reactions, 17 comments: setter not called for default value) | #70575 (closed not planned, 4 reactions, 7 comments: @export-ed variables set after _init) | #91882 (closed not planned, 1 reaction, 2 comments) | #30460 (closed 2020, 0 reactions, 17 comments: exported variables break setget methods that are ready-dependent) | godot-proposals#9639 (open, 6 reactions: wait for ready before set on exported properties in tool scripts)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/best_practices/godot_notifications.html "an exported property's value is again replaced by any value set in the Inspector, triggering the setter." | same page: "If a setter exists, it is not used." (initial value) | same page: "instantiating a script versus a scene may affect both the initialization and the number of times the engine calls the setter." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Initialization order) "When instantiating scenes and resources, the exported values are assigned." followed by "(Only for Node-derived classes) @onready variables are initialized."
evidence_source: scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:389 (node created with ClassDB::instantiate) | scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:496 (set_script: script instance, initializers, _init) | scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:567 (node->set for each stored property; runs setter) | scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:616 (node added to parent only after its own properties; children are created later in the same loop)
frequency: 6 GitHub issues/proposals found via reactions-sorted GraphQL searches (max 12 reactions) | one web search returned >=5 distinct forum.godotengine.org threads on this confusion (e.g. "The function set() is executed before _ready()", "When are export values set?", "Export variable set later than expected causing runtime errors")
status: by-design (documented); related reports closed not planned
fix_reason: The engine will always call ScriptInstance::set during SceneState instantiation, but the language can define a configure phase for its own properties (store injected values, defer setter side effects to enter-tree/ready) in the GDExtension script-instance set/notification callbacks; it cannot make the engine set properties after children exist.

title: _init with required parameters breaks scene instantiation, duplicate() and set_script()
description: The engine constructs script instances with zero arguments when loading scenes/resources, duplicating, or assigning a script, so a script whose _init has required parameters fails to construct; the error is only printed and the object continues without its script; PackedScene.instantiate() cannot pass constructor arguments.
example: `func _init(p_hp: int): hp = p_hp` on a scene root -> instantiate() logs "Error constructing a GDScriptInstance ... Method expected 1 argument(s), but called with 0" and returns a script-less node
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#1513 (open, 130 reactions, 41 comments: make it possible to pass arguments to PackedScene.instance()) | #27834 (closed 2020, 29 reactions, 10 comments: allow passing _init() arguments into instance()) | #67059 (closed, 0 reactions, 7 comments: exported resource whose _init takes a parameter is null at scene startup) | #28986 (open, 7 comments: script shadow-removed when _init(arg) + tool)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/best_practices/godot_notifications.html "_init() triggers before _enter_tree() or _ready(), but after a script creates and initializes its properties."
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:434 (instance_create calls _create_instance(nullptr, 0, ...): zero arguments) | modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:194-203 (_init call error detaches the script instance and only ERR_FAILs) | scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:389,496 (scene nodes created natively, then set_script) | scene/main/node.cpp:2838 and :3090-3092 (duplicate creates the native class then copies the script property)
frequency: godot-proposals#1513: 130 reactions (largest lifecycle proposal found); predecessor #27834: 29 reactions
fix_reason: The engine always constructs with zero arguments, but the language can forbid required constructor parameters on engine-instantiable Node/Resource types and offer a typed factory (instantiate, then call a language-level initializer with arguments before add_child) over public APIs.

title: Children's _ready runs before the parent's; enter_tree is top-down but ready is bottom-up
description: _enter_tree is called parent-first while _ready (and @onready initialization) is called child-first, so a child's _ready that reads the parent's @onready vars or state set in the parent's _ready sees null/defaults; sibling readiness depends on scene order.
example: child.gd: `func _ready(): get_parent().bar.max_value = 10` while parent has `@onready var bar = $Bar` -> bar is still null
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#5332 (open, 0 reactions, 22 comments: provide a way to modify order of _ready calls) | godot-proposals#553 (closed, 1 reaction, 6 comments: add _inverted_ready) | godot-proposals#14721 (open, 3 reactions: node_added_post_ready signal)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_node.html (_ready, class-reference text) "If the node has children, their _ready callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards." | same page (_enter_tree) "If the node has children, its _enter_tree callback will be called first, and then that of the children."
evidence_source: scene/main/node.cpp:326-336 (_propagate_ready recurses into children before NOTIFICATION_READY) | scene/main/node.cpp:360-381 (_propagate_enter_tree notifies self before children) | modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:1969-1971 (@onready initializers run only when _ready is called)
frequency: weak GitHub signal (proposals max 3 reactions; #5332 has 22 comments); forum frequency not measured
fix_reason: The engine order cannot change, but the language can type parent/sibling late fields as not-yet-initialized inside ready hooks and provide a second-phase hook run after the whole instantiated subtree is ready (scheduled from the owner's READY via notification or deferred call).

title: @onready fields are null until the first _ready, overwrite exported values, and break on await
description: @onready initializers run immediately before _ready (base class first), so they are null in _init, setters and _enter_tree and are not re-run on re-entry unless request_ready(); combining @onready with @export makes the default overwrite the inspector value (ONREADY_WITH_EXPORT, error by default); an await inside an @onready initializer suspends initialization and leaves later @onready fields null (#124692).
example: `@onready @export var target: Node = $Default` -> inspector value overwritten at ready
evidence_issues: #17596 (closed 2020, 14 reactions, 11 comments: expand onready keyword to export variables) | #62741 (closed 2026-09 as consistent behavior, 5 reactions, 8 comments: @onready @export breaks) | #63329 (closed 2024-05: base-class @onready initialized after derived; fixed) | #124692 (open 2026-10, 0 reactions: await in an @onready initializer leaves later @onready vars null) | #46233 (open, 2 reactions: get_node in a non-onready array initializer not caught)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html "GDScript has the @onready annotation, that defers initialization of a member variable until _ready() is called." | same page: "Applying @onready and any @export annotation to the same variable doesn't work as you might expect. The @onready annotation will cause the default value to be set after the @export takes effect and will override it"
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:1956-1971 (implicit ready initializers called from callp("_ready"), base script first) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h:94,154 (ONREADY_WITH_EXPORT, default ERROR) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h:93,153 (GET_NODE_DEFAULT_WITHOUT_ONREADY, default ERROR) | scene/main/node.cpp:334-337 (READY only once, so @onready not re-run); await-in-initializer behavior: unverified (needs repro)
frequency: 53 godot issues with "onready" in the title (GraphQL search, max 14 reactions) | forum thread "Am I misunderstanding how @onready works?" (web search)
status: partly mitigated (ONREADY_WITH_EXPORT error by default; base-first order fixed 2024); rest by-design; #124692 open
fix_reason: A typed language can model late-initialized fields with definite-initialization analysis, reject reads from setters/_init/_enter_tree, and reject export+late combinations and awaits in field initializers at compile time.

title: _ready runs once per node lifetime; re-adding or reparenting re-runs only enter/exit tree
description: After remove_child/add_child or reparent, _exit_tree/_enter_tree fire again but _ready and @onready do not unless request_ready() is called before re-adding, and request_ready() affects only that node, not its children; setup in _ready paired with teardown in _exit_tree becomes unbalanced.
example: `remove_child(a); add_child(a)` -> _enter_tree for a and its children, no _ready
evidence_issues: #17182 (closed 2019, 8 comments: _ready() only called in first add_child() for instanced scene) | godot-proposals#3290 (closed, 1 reaction, 23 comments: parameter for ready() to indicate first call)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_node.html (_ready, class-reference text) "Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, _ready will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with request_ready" | same page (request_ready) "This method only affects the current node. If the node's children also need to request ready, this method needs to be called for each one of them."
evidence_source: scene/main/node.cpp:334-337 (NOTIFICATION_READY only while data.ready_first) | scene/main/node.cpp:3616-3618 (request_ready sets ready_first) | scene/main/node.cpp:341-381 (enter-tree propagation runs on every add)
frequency: low on GitHub (closed reports; 23 comments on proposal #3290); documented
fix_reason: The language can expose explicit, distinct lifecycle hooks (first ready vs every enter/exit) and define field initialization independently of tree re-entry; the engine's single READY stays unchanged.

title: Changing a parent's children while it propagates enter/ready fails ("Parent node is busy setting up children")
description: While a node propagates enter-tree/ready/exit to its children it is blocked; add_child/add_sibling/move_child/remove_child on it from a child's _ready/_enter_tree (e.g., spawning into get_parent() or the scene root at startup) prints an error and does nothing, leaving the new node unparented (a leak unless freed); the fix is call_deferred.
example: child.gd `func _ready(): get_parent().add_child(Bullet.new())` -> ERROR: Parent node is busy setting up children, add_child() failed.
evidence_issues: 39 godot issues contain "busy setting up children" (GraphQL search; many are engine/editor-internal triggers), e.g. #77095 (closed 2024, 1 reaction, 30 comments) | #101410 (open, 3 comments) | #103511 (open: crash on changing scene with free() in _ready())
evidence_docs: - (no docs statement found; the error text itself says "Consider using add_child.call_deferred(child) instead.")
evidence_source: scene/main/node.cpp:325-330 (blocked++ while propagating ready to children) | scene/main/node.cpp:374-383 (same in _propagate_enter_tree) | scene/main/node.cpp:1721 (add_child ERR_FAIL_COND_MSG(data.blocked > 0, ...)) | scene/main/node.h:217,375-376 (data.blocked is private, _block/_unblock protected; no public accessor)
frequency: one web search for the exact message returned >=7 distinct threads (forum.godotengine.org, godotforums.org, ask.godotengine.org) | 39 GitHub issues mention the message
fix_reason: The runtime knows when it is dispatching enter/ready notifications to its own instances and can auto-defer or reject tree mutations then via public call_deferred; the exact per-node lock (Node::data.blocked) is private with no accessor even in C++, so a precise check needs an engine change.

title: References to freed objects: runtime errors on use, typed slots reject them, truthiness changed in 4.4
description: free() leaves every variable pointing at a "<Freed Object>"; calls and property access are runtime errors; passing it to a typed parameter or assigning it to a typed variable is a script error that aborts the function; `freed == null` and, since 4.4, `if freed:` are false, but code written for 3.x/4.0-4.3 assumed otherwise; is_instance_valid() is the documented check (IDs carry a 39-bit validator, so slot reuse is not a practical false positive in 4.x).
example: `var n := Node.new(); n.free(); take(n)` with `func take(x: Node)` -> script error "(previously freed) is not a subclass of the expected argument class"
evidence_issues: #85947 (open, 15 reactions, 18 comments: runtime error when passing a previously freed Object as a statically typed argument) | #110511 (open, 13 reactions, 10 comments: erasing a freed object from a typed array or dictionary fails) | #59816 (closed 2026-02, 9 reactions, 14 comments: inconsistent boolean of [Freed Object]; fixed by PR #93885, 4.4) | #101423 (open, 5 reactions: typed for-loop variable errors on invalid references) | #112166 (open, 2 reactions) | #123449 (open, 1 reaction)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_object.html (free, class-reference text) "Pre-existing references to the object become invalid, and any attempt to access them will result in a runtime error. Checking the references with is_instance_valid will return false."
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:558-563 (typed argument check fails for a freed object) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:1540 ("Trying to assign invalid previously freed instance.") | core/variant/variant.cpp:980-981 (is_zero true for a freed object, so it is falsy) | core/variant/variant_op.h:532-536 (Object == null compares the validated pointer) | core/object/object.h:884-891 (ObjectID = slot + 39-bit validator)
frequency: 9 godot issues with "previously freed" in the title | one web search returned >=8 distinct forum threads on "previously freed instance" errors
fix_reason: The language can type engine-object references as checked handles with an explicit alive/expired state (non-null types that cannot silently become dead) and implement liveness with public object_get_instance_from_id / is_instance_valid; no core change needed.

title: queue_free is deferred: the node stays alive, in the tree, processing and truthy until the end of the frame
description: After queue_free() the node stays valid until the SceneTree flushes its delete queue at the end of the process/physics frame; it still gets callbacks and signals, is_instance_valid() and `if node:` are true, so "already dead" logic can run twice; is_queued_for_deletion() must be checked separately and there is no "freeing" signal.
example: `enemy.queue_free(); print(is_instance_valid(enemy))` -> true
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#7441 (open, 23 reactions, 18 comments: emit a freeing signal when queue_free is called on a Node) | #84860 (closed, 2 reactions: memory leak when calling queue_free() before a SceneTreeTimer times out) | #80250 (closed not planned: deferred call on a previously freed instance)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_node.html (queue_free, class-reference text) "Unlike with Object.free, the node is not deleted instantly, and it can still be accessed before deletion." | same: "Note: The node will only be freed after all other deferred calls are finished."
evidence_source: scene/main/node.cpp:3518-3527 (queue_free -> SceneTree::queue_delete) | scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:736 (_flush_delete_queue after _process, timers and tweens) | scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:667 (same in physics_process) | core/object/object.cpp:1987 (is_queued_for_deletion is bound)
frequency: proposal #7441: 23 reactions | forum thread "Is there a way to check for ( recently ) freed object ?" (web search)
fix_reason: The language can treat queued-for-deletion as dead in its liveness checks and expose a dying hook using bound Object.is_queued_for_deletion and the script-instance notification callback; the deferral itself stays.

title: Destruction order: PREDELETE vs _exit_tree, and a RefCounted's self is unusable in PREDELETE
description: free() on a node in the tree sends PREDELETE to the script first, while the node is still in the tree with its children; then the Node handler removes it from the parent (subtree _exit_tree, children before parent) and deletes the children, whose PREDELETE comes after their exit; for RefCounted, PREDELETE runs after the count reached zero, self is a null instance and calling own methods errors or crashes; there is no reliable destructor.
example: RefCounted: `func _notification(w): if w == NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE: _cleanup()` -> null-instance call / editor crash (#80834)
evidence_issues: #6784 (open since 2016, 12 reactions, 32 comments: custom class extending Reference already freed when it receives NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE) | #80834 (open, 10 reactions, 11 comments: calling a class method on NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE crashes the editor) | #93287 (closed not planned, 2 comments: RefCounted PREDELETE runs after it is nullified) | #87151 (open: PREDELETE timing across nodes when deleting a branch is off)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_node.html (_exit_tree, class-reference text) "If the node has children, its _exit_tree callback will be called last, after all its children have left the tree."
evidence_source: core/object/object.cpp:140 (PREDELETE sent with p_reversed=true) | core/object/object.cpp:1009-1011 (reversed notification reaches the script instance first) | scene/main/node.cpp:304-312 (Node PREDELETE handler removes from parent, then memdeletes children) | scene/main/node.cpp:421-427 (_propagate_exit_tree: children first, then _exit_tree) | RefCounted self being null in PREDELETE: per #80834/#6784, unverified at line level
frequency: #6784 open 10 years with 32 comments; #80834 10 reactions
fix_reason: The runtime receives PREDELETE and the free callback of its own script instances (GDExtensionScriptInstanceNotification2 / GDExtensionScriptInstanceFree) and can run a language-defined destructor over its own fields without re-referencing self; the engine's subtree teardown order cannot be changed.

title: RefCounted reference cycles leak (no cycle collector), including self-capturing callables and awaits
description: Two RefCounted objects that reference each other, or a RefCounted that stores a Callable/lambda/connection bound to itself, are never freed; GDScript has only untyped WeakRef via weakref(), and leaks show only as object counts or "ObjectDB instances leaked at exit".
example: `a.other = b; b.other = a` -> neither is freed while the game runs
evidence_issues: #7038 (open since 2016, 8 reactions, 18 comments: memory leak with circular reference in GDScript) | godot-proposals#9174 (open, 35 reactions: typed WeakRefs in GDScript) | godot-proposals#540 (open, 17 reactions: better orphan nodes and memory-leak tracking) | #121618 (open, 0 reactions: chained awaits result in cyclic references and leak) | #81210 (open, 8 reactions, 19 comments; discussion of self-reference through callables on RefCounted)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_refcounted.html (class-reference text) "RefCounted instances caught in a cyclic reference will not be freed automatically." | same: "To prevent this, one of the references in the cycle can be made weak with @GlobalScope.weakref."
evidence_source: unverified (no single line; reference counting without cycle detection is stated by the docs) | core/object/ref_counted.cpp:67 (get_reference_count is bound, usable by a runtime)
frequency: #7038: 18 comments over 10 years | proposal #9174: 35 reactions
fix_reason: The language can add typed weak references and ownership annotations, flag self-capturing closures stored on RefCounted at compile time, and could run a cycle collector over objects whose fields it owns (refcounts readable via bound get_reference_count); references held by engine code stay opaque.

title: Nodes removed from the tree, or never added, are not freed (orphan-node leaks)
description: Node is not reference-counted: remove_child(), replace_by(), or dropping the last variable to an unparented Node.new() or instantiated scene leaves the node alive forever; leaks show only via Performance.OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT / print_orphan_nodes, and get_orphan_node_ids works only in debug builds.
example: `remove_child(n); n = null` -> node leaked
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#540 (open, 17 reactions: better orphan nodes and memory leak tracking) | #16815 (closed, 2 reactions, 10 comments: add warning messages for orphan nodes on debug builds) | #107654 (open: duplicate variable names cause orphaned nodes without error messages) | #47581 (open: OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT does not print the real number)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_node.html (remove_child, class-reference text) "The node, along with its children, are not deleted. To delete a node, see queue_free." | same (replace_by): "The replaced node is removed from the tree, but it is not deleted. To prevent memory leaks, store a reference to the node in a variable, or use Object.free."
evidence_source: doc/classes/Node.xml:835 (remove_child: node and children are not deleted) | doc/classes/Node.xml:510-511 (get_orphan_node_ids only in debug builds) | absence of any automatic free path: unverified at line level
frequency: low-moderate (proposal #540: 17 reactions)
fix_reason: Static analysis can flag Node values that are created or removed but neither parented nor freed on all paths, and the runtime can track unparented nodes it created and report or free them when its last handle drops; making Node reference-counted would be E.

title: A coroutine is silently abandoned when its object, or the awaited signal's emitter, is freed
description: When the instance running an await is freed its pending function states are cleared: code after the await never runs (no finally/cleanup) and callers awaiting it are never resumed and get no error; awaiting a signal of an object that is freed without emitting likewise never resumes; locals of abandoned coroutines leaked until 4.7; a RefCounted is not kept alive by its own pending await (#81210).
example: `var r = await worker.job()` then `worker.free()` -> nothing after the await runs in either function, no error
evidence_issues: #24311 (closed 2023, 33 reactions, 21 comments: destroying an object running a coroutine should interrupt it; PR #65910 (4.0) made it stop silently) | #99383 (open, 1 reaction, 6 comments: freeing a node with a running Tween or awaited coroutine leaks; locals leak fixed by PR #116711, 4.7, via #116706) | #81210 (open, 8 reactions, 19 comments: RefCounted objects with outstanding await can be destroyed) | #74449 (closed, 4 reactions: await GDScriptFunctionState leaks) | #79669 (closed, 5 reactions: SceneTreeTimer leaked when awaiting while quitting)
evidence_docs: - (gdscript_basics "Awaiting signals or coroutines" does not say what happens to a pending await when its object is freed)
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:2089-2091 (GDScriptInstance destructor clears pending function states) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_function.cpp:335-349 (clear(): disconnects and clears the stack, never resumes or emits completed) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:2585-2586 (awaiting a coroutine = awaiting its state's completed signal, so the caller hangs) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:2642 (await is a one-shot connection bound to the state; dropped with the emitter) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_function.cpp:281-283 (debug error only if resumed after the instance is gone)
frequency: #24311: 33 reactions (top result of the reactions-sorted "await freed" search) | 5+ related issues
status: partly fixed (silent stop since 4.0, PR #65910; locals leak fixed in 4.7, PR #116711); no cleanup or cancellation semantics
fix_reason: A language with its own coroutine runtime can bind tasks to an owner and, on the owner's PREDELETE (script-instance notification callback), deliver cancellation that runs finally/defer blocks and fails awaiting callers; no core change needed.

title: Coroutines cannot be cancelled and async functions are re-entrant by default
description: There is no way to cancel a pending await from outside; calling an async function again while an earlier call is suspended starts a second execution that interleaves with the first over shared member state (double animations, stale flags), so users write generation counters or flags by hand.
example: `func flash(): modulate = RED; await get_tree().create_timer(0.2).timeout; modulate = WHITE` called twice 0.1 s apart -> the first call's resume cuts the second flash short
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#8838 (open, 39 reactions: make coroutines cancelable) | godot-proposals#6243 (open, 97 reactions: or/and in await statements, used for timeouts and races) | godot-proposals#13597 (open, 10 reactions: await all/any) | godot-proposals#5673 (open, 16 reactions: replace GDScriptFunctionState in await coroutines) | godot-proposals#11909 (open, 11 reactions: cancelable signal awaits, C#)
evidence_docs: - (no cancellation API in gdscript_basics "Awaiting signals or coroutines")
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:2603-2642 (each await creates an independent GDScriptFunctionState with its own stack copy and one-shot connection; no handle is given to callers for cancellation)
frequency: #8838: 39 reactions | #6243: 97 reactions (composition/timeouts)
fix_reason: Structured concurrency (task handles, cancel, scoped tasks, restart/drop policies for re-entrant calls) is purely a design choice for the language's own coroutines.

title: A function silently becomes a coroutine; calling it without await is allowed and not warned by default
description: Any function containing await becomes a coroutine; calling it as a statement runs it to its first await and continues the caller (fire-and-forget), and the MISSING_AWAIT warning added in 4.6 is off by default; await on a value that is neither a signal nor a coroutine returns immediately (only a warning), so adding or removing an await in a callee silently changes caller timing.
example: `func open_door(): await anim.animation_finished` ; caller `open_door(); enter_room()` -> enters before the door has opened
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#12653 (closed completed, 9 reactions, 10 comments: opt-in warning for calling a coroutine without await; PR #107936, 4.6) | godot-proposals#11094 (open, 13 reactions: @must_await annotation) | godot-proposals#3901 (open, 11 reactions: annotate a function to always await at call site)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html "If you don't depend on the result, you can just call it asynchronously, which won't stop execution and won't make the current function a coroutine." | same: "If you use await with an expression that isn't a signal nor a coroutine, the value will be returned immediately and the function won't give the control back to the caller"
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h:76,136 (MISSING_AWAIT, default IGNORE) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h:75,135 (REDUNDANT_AWAIT, default WARN) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:2591-2596 (non-signal await stores the value and continues synchronously)
frequency: 3 proposals, 33 reactions in total
fix_reason: Make asynchrony part of the function type (async marker or Task[T] return) and require an explicit await or explicit spawn at every call site; reject await on non-awaitable types statically.

title: Signal parameters are not type- or arity-checked at connect or emit
description: connect() accepts any callable regardless of parameter count or types, and emit()/emit_signal() accept any number and type of arguments even for signals declared with typed parameters; mismatches surface only at emit time, per connection, as printed errors (that handler is skipped), or not at all when the handler is untyped; awaiting a multi-argument signal yields an untyped Array.
example: `signal hit(damage: int)` ; `hit.connect(func(a, b): pass)` and `hit.emit("x")` both compile
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#2557 (open, 134 reactions, 8 comments: type hints for signal parameters; maintainer comment: "signals are still untyped. You can pass any number of arguments of any type to emit(), and this will not cause an error (only in callbacks)") | #12450 (open since 2017, 7 reactions, 8 comments: warn on connected functions without correct argument count) | godot-proposals#8987 (closed not planned, 2 reactions: log error when a signal is called with incompatible types) | #86609 (open, 4 reactions) and #62982 (closed, 4 reactions): typed handler conversion errors
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Awaiting signals or coroutines) "If there is more than one parameter, the awaited value will be of type Array"

title: Editor-made signal connections name the handler as a string in .tscn; a renamed or deleted handler is silently ignored
description: Connections made in the editor are saved as [connection signal=... from=... to=... method="name"] and recreated at load without checking the method; if the handler is renamed or deleted the connection still loads and emit skips it silently because the Callable is invalid; the editor warns only for the currently edited scene while its script is open, and the 4.8 symbol-rename tool does not update scenes.
example: rename `_on_timer_timeout` to `_on_timer_done` -> the timer fires, nothing happens, nothing is logged
evidence_issues: #123958 (open, 6 reactions, 4 comments: symbol-renaming tracker: "Method and signal connections are not renamed in scenes" and "a warning can't be feasibly implemented") | godot-proposals#899 (closed by PR #117949 in 4.8, 520 reactions: rename-symbol tooling, scripts only)
evidence_docs: - (no docs statement found on stale editor connections)
evidence_source: scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:747,763 (Callable(target, method name) connected with CONNECT_PERSIST, no existence check) | core/object/object.cpp:1590-1594 (connect only checks the target object for standard callables) | core/variant/callable.cpp:155 (is_valid requires has_method) | core/object/object.cpp:1328-1331 (invalid callables skipped silently during emit) | editor/script/script_text_editor.cpp:970-982 (missing-connected-method warning only for the edited scene)
frequency: rename-tooling proposal #899: 520 reactions (general); the scene gap itself is tracked only in #123958
fix_reason: The toolchain can parse .tscn [connection] entries and check method existence and signature against the target script, and rename refactors can update scenes; a runtime can also validate incoming connections at ready via bound Object.get_incoming_connections (core/object/object.cpp:1969).

title: Connection identity: duplicate connect is an error, binds are ignored, lambdas cannot be disconnected without the original reference
description: Connecting the same callable twice prints an error and returns ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER unless CONNECT_REFERENCE_COUNTED is used; identity ignores bound arguments, so connecting one method twice with different binds fails; lambdas compare by reference, so is_connected/disconnect with a textually identical lambda fail and an anonymous connection can only be removed via get_connections() or by freeing its object.
example: `hit.connect(func(d): print(d))` ; `hit.disconnect(func(d): print(d))` -> "Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection"
evidence_issues: #63038 (open, 5 reactions, 13 comments: "Signal is already connected" when callable has different binds) | #42161 (open, 10 reactions, 14 comments: "Signal already connected" error for inherited scenes, 3.2)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_object.html (connect, class-reference text) "A signal can only be connected once to the same Callable. If the signal is already connected, this method returns ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER and generates an error, unless the signal is connected with CONNECT_REFERENCE_COUNTED."
evidence_source: core/object/object.cpp:1625-1631 (duplicate check on the base comparator, binds ignored) | core/object/object.cpp:1713 (disconnect of a nonexistent connection errors) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_lambda_callable.cpp:37-39,163-165 (lambda callables compared by reference only)
frequency: low on GitHub (max 10 reactions) | forum: godotforums thread "Is there a proper way to connect a lambda to a signal" (web search)
fix_reason: The language can make connect return a subscription handle (disposed explicitly or with its owner) and define idempotent or keyed connections, implemented over bound connect/disconnect and CONNECT_REFERENCE_COUNTED.

title: SceneTree.create_timer keeps running while the game is paused and is not tied to the awaiting node
description: get_tree().create_timer(t) defaults process_always=true, so `await get_tree().create_timer(1).timeout` continues while the tree is paused (unlike Timer nodes and node-bound tweens), and the timer belongs to the SceneTree, so the node's process_mode does not affect it.
example: `get_tree().paused = true; await get_tree().create_timer(0.2).timeout` -> resumes while paused
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#9924 (open, 16 reactions: make create_timer's process_always default to false; "a source of headaches and bugs over and over again") | godot-proposals#4908 (open, 46 reactions, 22 comments: add Node.create_timer) | #7656 (closed: create_timer() doesn't pause) | #116443 (open: embedded-window suspend does not stop awaited coroutines)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_scenetree.html (create_timer, class-reference text; default process_always=true) "If process_always is false, the timer will be paused when setting SceneTree.paused to true." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/pausing_games.html "This means that, by default, when the game is paused every node will be paused."
evidence_source: scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:1942 (create_timer bound with DEFVAL(true) for process_always)
frequency: #9924: 16 reactions | #4908: 46 reactions
fix_reason: A standard-library wait/timer can default to pause-aware, owner-bound timing using public create_timer(t, false), Timer or Tween APIs, and be cancelled with its owner.

title: Timer nodes tick at most once per frame, start() fails outside the tree, and depend on frame rate and time_scale
description: Timer subtracts delta once per process or physics frame and emits timeout at most once per frame, so wait times below a frame are quantized (a 1 ms repeating timer fires once per frame); start() before the node is in the tree only prints an error; timers scale with Engine.time_scale.
example: `t.wait_time = 0.001` -> one timeout per frame, not 1000 per second
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#10879 (closed not planned, 5 reactions, 12 comments: Frame option for Timer) | godot-proposals#3386 (open, 5 reactions: synchronize Timer to delta/FPS) | #107203 (open, 6 comments: Timer that ticks on physics and ignores time scale is wrong)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_timer.html (wait_time, class-reference text) "Timers can only process once per physics or process frame (depending on the process_callback). An unstable framerate may cause the timer to end inconsistently, which is especially noticeable if the wait time is lower than roughly 0.05 seconds." | same (start) "Fails if the timer is not inside the scene tree."
evidence_source: scene/main/timer.cpp:60-67 (a single if: at most one timeout per tick) | scene/main/timer.cpp:120 (start fails when not inside the tree) | scene/main/timer.cpp:75-76 (physics ticking with ignore_time_scale uses the process step, cf. #107203)
frequency: low on GitHub; documented
fix_reason: The standard library can provide timers that catch up (fire N times or report elapsed count) and queue start until enter-tree, built on _process/_physics_process and bound APIs; the engine Timer node stays as is.

title: Static variable initialization follows script load order; cycles misbehave and statics reset on reload
description: Static initializers and _static_init run when a script is loaded or reloaded, so their order follows whichever script loads first; a cycle between static initializers sees a half-loaded script, an instance _init can run before its class's _static_init (#82141), statics are re-initialized on every script reload (old values restored only in editor keep-state reloads), and scripts with statics are never unloaded.
example: a.gd `static var x = load("res://b.gd").y` ; b.gd `static var y = load("res://a.gd").x` -> b sees a null script during a's load
evidence_issues: #82141 (open, 2 reactions, 4 comments: a class _init can be called before its _static_init) | #115996 (open, 4 reactions: silent preload() failure across class_name/autoload load order) | #81250 (open, 2 reactions: static vars not initialized on scripts preloaded by tool scripts) | #105667 (open, 4 comments: static variables do not update during hot reload) | #77098 (closed, 3 reactions: issues with static variables)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html (Static variables) "having static variables in a script prevents it from being unloaded even if there are no more instances of that class and no other references left." | same: "Currently, due to a bug, scripts are never freed, even if @static_unload annotation is used."
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:675-678 (_static_init runs the static initializer) | modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:897-898 (run at the end of every GDScript::reload) | modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:905-906 (old static data restored only with p_keep_state in TOOLS builds) | core/io/resource_loader.cpp:1049-1056 (a cyclic load on the loading thread returns a null resource with ERR_BUSY); that this path is the one hit by static-initializer cycles: unverified (needs repro)
frequency: low (5 open issues, max 4 reactions)
fix_reason: The language can define deterministic static initialization (lazy per-member init with cycle detection, or module-graph order) and reload semantics in its own ScriptExtension, and reject static-initializer cycles at compile time.
